2.2.2 The cloth shall be rendered mothproof. employed for the purpose may be dieldrin or DDT.

The

proofing agent

NOTE - Proofing agents other than those prcscribcd ahovc may be used subject Proofing agent shall, however, be of to agreement between the buyer and the seller. such a nature end compositirn that its required amount can be estimated by a chemical test.

2.2.3 The cloth when visually examined both against light and on surface shall not contain more than one objectionable flaw per II m length. The objectionable flaws shall be those which strike immediately the eyes of the person examining the cloth at a distance of 50 cm and shall be deemed to include:
a) missing ends and picks; b) floats; c) cuts and holes; d) stains; e) weft bars and warp section marks; f) big slubs, knots and specks; g) dyeing defects ( streaks, patches, etc ); and h) thick and thin places.

2.2.3.1 All objectionable flaws shall be marked by means of a thread sewn in the selvedge opposite the flaw, and an allowance of 10 cm shall be given for each flaw. Only one selvedge shall be used for tagging.
2.2.3.2 A' reference these defects, 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 The constructional Table 2. particulars of cloth shall conform to those given in may be made to IS : 4125-1967* for details of

3.2 Colour fastness ratings and other requirements of cloth shall conform to those given in Table 3. 4. SEALED SAMPLE

4.1 If, in order to illustrate or specify the general appearance, feel, shade and finish, etc, of a particular variety of cloth, a sample has been agreed upon and sealed, the supply shall be in ,conformity with the sample in such respects.

4.1.1 The custody of- the sealed sample shall be a matter of prior agreement between the buyer and the seller.

5. MARKING 5.1 The cloth shall be marked with the following:
a) Name of the material, b) The legend ' All wool ' or `Blended wool ' as the case may be, in latter case the composition of blend be also indicated; c) Variety number and the legend `Ref ISS : 677'; d) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade mark; e) Month and year of manufacture; and f) Length and width of the piece.

Certification

Marking

The product may also be marked with Standard Mark. 5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be g&ted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6. PACKING 6.1 The cloth shall be packed in bales or cases in conformity with the procedure laid down either in IS : 32-1971* or in IS : 741-1971t as required. 6.2 Alternatively, the cloth may be packed according to the details below when specifically agreed to between the buyer and the seller: given

Each piece shall be suitably folded in a rectangular form or wrapped on cardboard or strawboard of suitable size and thickness. Each piece then shall .be wrapped with polyethylene film of minimum 40 microns thickness or alternatively kraft paper. The edges of the kraft paper or polyethylene film shall be gummed or sealed. Alternatively, each piece may be tied with a twine at least at 2 places. Such pieces, in a suitable number, shall then be enclosed in an outer layer of heavy tee jute cloth preferably conforming to IS : 3751-1966$ to form compact bales. The bales shall be made secure by cross hooping the steel strips at right angles to both the length and width of the baIe. The gross weight of the bale shall not normally exceed 40 kg. All packing materials shall conform to IS : 741-19711_. 7. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA

( Table 3 )
METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF WATER REPELLANCY OF CLOTH A-l. TEST SPECIMENS A-IS Draw one specimen measuring piece in the sample under test.
A-2. PROCEDURE A-2.1 Clamp one test specimen on a glass plate incIined at an angle of 45". Allow water to drop from a glass jet on to the face of the t&t specimen from a height of 2 m at the rate of 18 drops per minute, adjusting the size of the jet and the flow of water so that 18 f 1 drops of water representing a volume of 1 f 0'05 ml are discharged every minute. A-2.2 During 30 minutes from the start of the test, examine from time to time the back of the test specimen and observe whether water penetrates through the test specimen or not. A-2.3 Repeat the test with the remaining test specimens. approximately

20 x 25 cm from each
